comment: Dr Seeley is an incredible professor. She is so passionate and knowledgable about the subject. Took this class as a gen ed and it was challenging. Lots of readings and participation is super important. History of slavery is not an easy subject to teach but she made it interesting and gave me many new perspectives. Gives good feedback on papers.

Dr. Seeley demonstrates expertise across a range of topics and facilitates thoughtful discussions on challenging subjects, such as slavery. She forms an environment where every voice is heard, fostering respectful and engaging conversations. Be prepared for 20-40 pages of reading per class, and take the time to prepare for in-class discussions.

Dr. Seeley is truly one of the nicest professor I have encountered at UR so far. She genuinely cares about her students and is so invested in what she is teaching. She is so accessible outside of class to discuss upcoming papers and always wants to try and help whenever a student asks. Make sure to participate in discussions!

Professor Seeley is AMAZING. She pushes her students intellectually while still offering assistance if we need it. She truly wants everyone to become more aware of the issues regarding slavery and its past, especially in the current racial climate. You can tell that she cares about her students and also wants them to learn as much as possible.

Dr. Seeley is an engaging professor. Her courses are well designed and she tries to make them interesting to non history majors, too. She was my summer fellowship advisor and was very helpful. Upper level courses can be pretty reading heavy, but that's typical for history. Discussions are lively, grading is fair, and she gives good feedback.

Never liked history classes just needed this for the gen ed requirement. Dr Seeley teaches the class in a way that makes you interested to learn about it. Our topic was Slavery in Virginia which I feel is very relevant to anyone attending Richmond. Lots of reading though but she's a very fair grader and gives good feedback. Oh and she's hot

Dr. Seeley is a good professor and knows her stuff, but she is very hard on papers for a history gen-ed. Her feedback is helpful but it becomes difficult to actually get a decent grade. Each class is participation based and there are a few papers.

Doctor Seeley is a great teacher and has an engaging class. She's a tough grader on papers but she always looks to help you improve on the next. There is a substantial amount of reading, but if you do it and participate in class, you will do fine in the class.

Professor Seeley's class is very interesting and goes by super fast. She is very helpful on papers, although she will tell you it's great and you will probably get a B. She loves giving out B's. Only three papers, a short final, and minimal reading though. I would recommend her class.
